summary: We consider the problem of computing observables beyond the spectrum in the open XXZ spin chain with the most generic integrable boundary conditions. For such boundaries, the residual u(1) symmetry is broken and the familiar Baxter TQ equation describing the spectrum becomes inhomogeneous, placing the model outside the realm of existing approaches to correlation functions and form factors. We show that the Functional Separation of Variables method, so far developed mainly for rational, (quasi-)periodic spin chains, is largely insensitive to these modifications, and works equally well for diagonal and generic boundaries. Using this method, we compute exact determinant expressions for a prototypical example of form factors in open-boundary systems, namely the longitudinal and transverse boundary-spin one-point functions in arbitrary Hamiltonian eigenstates at finite system size. No constraint relating the two boundary configurations and no reference state are required. We verify the resulting formulae against direct finite-volume diagonalisation.

title: Analytical solution of electromagnetic heating in a stratified absorbing medium
summary: We consider the temperature evolution in a skin tissue when it is exposed to an electromagnetic wave. The heating is caused by the absorbed power as the electromagnetic wave attenuates inside the skin. In many applications, the characteristic depth of attenuation is small in comparison with the lateral size of the electromagnetic beam. Because of this separation of length scales, the lateral heat conduction is negligible at leading order. Previously, we studied electromagnetic heating in a skin of a single homogeneous layer. We derived the leading-term analytical solution and the asymptotic corrections up to the second order for lateral heat conduction and for oblique incidence. In this study, we derive the analytical solution in the case of perpendicular incidence on a stratified skin tissue with a layer-specific profile for electromagnetic attenuation. It should be emphasized that in the current study, the heat capacity and conductivity are still uniform over the entire skin tissue; only the electromagnetic attenuation is stratified resulting in a layer-specific heating profile.

title: Counterexamples to the total-current Hohenberg-Kohn conjecture
summary: The total-current Hohenberg-Kohn conjecture asserts that the ground-state particle density and total current determine the scalar potential up to an additive constant and the vector potential up to a gauge transformation. We give three counterexamples for two spinless fermions in the physically relevant setting of three spatial dimensions. In each, a Hamiltonian $H^{v,\mathbf{A}}$ has a nondegenerate ground state with identically zero total current but nonzero magnetic field. Complex conjugation then yields a second Hamiltonian $H^{v,-\mathbf{A}}$, with the same scalar potential and interaction, whose ground state has the same density and the same zero current, while the magnetic field is reversed. The first two examples are noninteracting. One is explicit, with a smooth bounded vector potential and a Gaussian density. The other has smooth bounded scalar and vector potentials in the standard potential spaces. The third example has Coulomb repulsion with unit coupling, an isotropic harmonic scalar potential, and Dirac monopole fields of magnetic charge $\pm 1/2$. The monopole example uses vector potentials defined on separate spatial patches, since these fields are not curls of globally defined smooth vector potentials.

title: Continuous and Differentiable Neural Network Representations of the Surfzone Sea-Surface from Lidar Point Clouds
summary: Ocean waves are often analyzed via sea-surface observations. Multi-beam scanning lidar enables two-dimensional measurements of the water surface $\eta(x,y)$ via sequenced point clouds of sea-surface elevation. Point cloud data, however, have to be gridded, interpolated, or mapped for use in wave analysis. We present and test a method for creating a continuous and differentiable (space and time), but grid-free, representation of the sea-surface from time sequenced lidar point clouds. We use a specific neural network architecture, a SIREN, to represent the sea-surface and to train the network on spatiotemporal 60~s of lidar data collected by a gas-electric UAS (drone) hovering over large (4 m), breaking waves in Monterey, California. The trained SIREN allows estimation of the sea-surface and its derivatives at any location and time. SIREN sea-surface representations tend to filter the highest wave number variability (splash-up and sea-spray). SIREN errors are comparable to instrument errors and insensitive to local data density. The reliability and reproducibility of our approach is tested by training two SIRENs independently on the same data. Differences between the two independent SIRENs are comparable to instrument error, but increase in data-poor regions. SIRENs' potential for directional wave analysis is demonstrated by computing spatial and temporal derivatives and by estimating wave velocity from a SIREN-generated space-time slice of the sea-surface.

title: Two routes to the Hadamard condition
summary: In quantum field theory on curved spacetime, the Hadamard condition is often presented as a necessary condition on 'physically reasonable', 'vacuum-like' states of linear quantum fields, and plays a central role in many theoretical and foundational applications - ranging from proofs of the renormalizability of Wick polynomials to derivations of the Hawking temperature. In this paper, I strengthen, generalise, and bring under technical control two popular motivations for the Hadamard condition - one which appeals to the role of Hadamard states in defining physical quantities such as Wick polynomials and the expectation value of the stress-energy operator on general curved spacetime backgrounds, and one which appeals to the equivalence principle. This clarifies the role and status of the Hadamard condition, including its relationship to the equivalence principle, to well-definedness of physical quantities such as Wick polynomials and the expectation value of the stress-energy operator, and the sense in which Hadamard states are 'vacuum-like'.

title: Phonon Dispersion Relation in Weakly Coupled Bose Gas Beyond Bogoliubov Approximation
summary: We study the quasiparticle dispersion relation for a homogeneous Bose gas in a large cubic box with periodic boundary conditions at zero temperature. Inspired by the Bogoliubov method, we rearrange the usual Bose gas Hamiltonian in a form adapted to perturbation theory in the weak-coupling regime, both in the canonical and grand-canonical setting. We compute the first non-trivial corrections to the dispersion relation in both settings. We show that for small momenta they are linear in the absolute value of the momentum. Thus, in this approximation phonons have a well-defined velocity, which we compute.

title: Half-delocalization for semiclassical measures of split higher-dimensional quantum cat maps
summary: We study quantum cat maps on multidimensional tori and prove an optimal lower bound for the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy of their semiclassical measures under the hypothesis that the dynamics splits over the rationals. This is the first instance of such a bound for a dynamical system with multiple positive Lyapunov exponents. The proof is based on a new notion of conditional quantum dynamical entropy and a careful study of the multiple Ehrenfest time adapted to the dynamics.

title: The concentration conjecture for Dirac--Coulomb operators
summary: We prove the concentration conjecture for the three-dimensional Dirac operator with mass $m>0$ and an attractive Coulomb potential generated by finitely many point charges. For a fixed total charge $G\in(0,1]$, the lowest eigenvalue in the spectral gap is at least $m\sqrt{1-G^2}$, with equality precisely when all the charge is concentrated at one point. The critical one-center operator is understood as its distinguished extension. The result also extends to arbitrary nonnegative finite charge measures. The proof uses a strict two-center estimate for the weighted free Dirac resolvent and a Birman-Schwinger comparison. We establish the two-center estimate through an auxiliary axial operator, combining a zero-energy bound and a scalar resolvent estimate with a radial decomposition, an angular Schur complement, and exact polynomial inequalities.

title: The $b\bar{b}c\bar{c}$ Fully Heavy Tetraquark at the LHC and the FCC: Multimodal Fragmentation and Observability
comment: 49 pages, 8 figures, LHAPDF release of the TQ4Qhf1.0 fragmentation-function set with uncertainties at this https URL
summary: We investigate the production of the all-heavy mixed-flavor $b\bar b c\bar c$ tetraquark through a multimodal fragmentation setup combining direct-multiquark and scalar-diquark mechanisms. Standard Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi (DGLAP) evolution is applied while preserving threshold consistency through the Heavy-Flavor NonRelativistic evolution (HF-NRevo) scheme. The resulting fragmentation functions (FFs) are then embedded into hybrid high-energy and collinear factorization at next-to-leading order for semi-inclusive tetraquark-plus-jet production. We compare the two mechanisms through rapidity-separation distributions at the 14 TeV High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) and at the 100 TeV Future Circular Collider (FCC), finding a clear phenomenological preference for the direct-multiquark channel over the scalar-diquark mode. Integrated cross sections and expected event yields provide favorable production-level prospects for future searches at the HL-LHC, with substantially enhanced statistics at FCC energies. These results establish a quantitative connection between microscopic formation mechanisms and the prospective observability of the $b\bar b c\bar c$ tetraquark at present and future hadron colliders.

title: Flavor decomposition of electromagnetic multipole moments in $[q_1q_2][\bar q_3 \bar c]$ tetraquarks: Light-quark analogs of $T_{cs1}(2900)^0$ with $J^P = 1^+$
comment: 12 pages, 5 tables,1 figure. The version is accepted for publication in Physics Letters B
summary: We present a systematic study of the magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole moments of compact $[q_1 q_2][\bar q_3 \bar c]$ tetraquark states with quantum numbers $J^P = 1^+$, in the diquark--antidiquark picture and within the light-cone QCD sum rule framework. By performing a flavor decomposition across all admissible $u/d$ configurations, we show that the charm-quark contribution to the electromagnetic moments vanishes algebraically at the operator level -- a structural feature of the specific spin organization adopted here, in which the heavy antiquark resides in a pseudoscalar antidiquark, distinct from the dynamical $1/m_c$ suppression operative in alternative compact constructions and in hadronic molecules. The magnetic moments follow a coherent light-flavor pattern -- positive for $uu$-, negative for $dd$-, and suppressed for mixed-flavor diquarks -- and the quadrupole moments are non-zero throughout, corresponding, in the customary geometrical interpretation, to intrinsically deformed charge distributions. We further identify the dimensionless multipole ratio $\mathcal{D}/\mu$ as a structural observable, independent of the normalization of the interpolating current, which probes the relative geometry of the spin-current and charge distributions complementary to the absolute moments. Taken together, the algebraic decoupling of the charm contribution and the operator-level distinction it implies among different singly-heavy tetraquark architectures constitute methodological signatures that discriminate among the corresponding internal organizations and, to the extent that a physical candidate is dominated by one of them, among compact and molecular interpretations.

title: From Harmonic Oscillators to Multiplicity Distributions in Particle Production Processes
summary: We propose an oscillator framework of studying multi-particle production processes using the information theory approach. For a system of degenerate oscillators, we derive the negative binomial distribution (NBD) and its nonadditive generalization represented as gNBD. We observe that gNBD derived from nonadditive statistics describes data in higher multiplicity region, thereby providing an alternative for the multi-component distributions used in phenomenological studies. We also generalize our framework for non-degenerate oscillators and encounter a Lerch-type generalization of the Barnes zeta function that, to the best of our knowledge, has not been studied in the context of nonadditive statistics and multiplicity studies before.

title: Partial reconstruction of the decay $B_{s}^{0}\rightarrow ϕ(K^{+}K^{-})η' (π^{+}π^{-}η)$
summary: The decay $B_s^0 \to \phi(K^+K^-)\eta'(\pi^+\pi^-\eta)$ is of particular interest in flavour physics because in the Standard Model it proceeds predominantly through the quark transition $\bar{b} \to \bar{s}s\bar{s}$. However, the reconstruction of this decay is experimentally challenging due to the presence of the neutral $\eta$ particle, which significantly reduces the overall reconstruction efficiency. In this study, the feasibility of using the partial reconstruction technique to reconstruct the invariant mass of the $B_s^0$ meson without explicitly detecting the $\eta$ particle is investigated. Monte Carlo simulated events corresponding to an FCC-ee environment are used, and the effects of detector momentum and vertex resolutions on the reconstruction performance are examined. The results show that improved vertex resolution substantially improves the global reconstructed mass response and partial-reconstruction efficiency, while improvements in momentum resolution are manifested primarily through a narrowing of the fitted central DCB component. These findings suggest that future high-luminosity $e^+e^-$ colliders such as FCC-ee could effectively exploit the partial reconstruction technique to study rare decay modes containing undetected neutral particles.

title: Probing the $τ$ anomalous magnetic and electric dipole moments in photon-induced $γγ\toτ^+τ^-$ production at the FCC-hh
summary: The sensitivity of the FCC-hh to the anomalous magnetic moment $a_\tau$ and the electric dipole moment $d_\tau$ of the $\tau$ lepton is studied in photon-induced $\gamma\gamma\to\tau^+\tau^-$ production with both $\tau$ leptons decaying hadronically. Central exclusive (elastic) signal events, in which both protons remain intact, are generated with MadGraph5_aMC@NLO using a FeynRules UFO model of the anomalous $\gamma\tau\tau$ vertex merged with the TauDecay model, so that the $\tau$ decays and their spin correlations are included in the matrix element. Single- and double-dissociative production is estimated with SuperChic and added to the elastic signal with its own coupling dependence and with normalisation and shape uncertainties of 25%. Pythia 8 decays the unstable hadrons in the signal, decays the $\tau$ leptons and simulates the parton shower and hadronisation in the backgrounds, and hadronises the dissociated protons. Signal and backgrounds are passed through the Delphes simulation of the FCC-hh detector. Hadronic $\tau$ decays are reconstructed from particle-flow tracks and photons with an algorithm based on the hadrons-plus-strips approach, with an efficiency of 73.4% within the acceptance. Requiring no additional tracks from the $\tau$ vertices retains part of the dissociative contribution and reduces the Drell-Yan and $\gamma\gamma\to WW$ backgrounds to 0.9% of the SM yield. The couplings are constrained from the shape of the total transverse mass distribution. For a centre-of-mass energy of 84 TeV and 30 ab$^{-1}$, the expected 95% CL limits are $-3.38\times10^{-4} < a_\tau < 3.36\times10^{-4}$ and $|d_\tau| < 1.88\times10^{-18}\,e\,$cm, about an order of magnitude beyond the current bounds. Results are also given for FCC-hh scenarios between 72 and 120 TeV and for an optimistic detector parametrisation.

title: Automation of amplitude-level QED resummation with ACRAIC
summary: Precision electroweak predictions for future $e^+e^-$ colliders will require levels of precision unmatched in collider physics and the modelling of multiple-photon emissions, and the exponentiation of the associated logarithms needs to be carefully considered. The Yennie-Frautschi-Suura theorem subtracts the infrared singularities to all orders and exponentiates them, leaving infrared-finite remainders which can be calculated order-by-order. Coherent exponentiation performs this subtraction at the amplitude level, preserving the interference between emissions, but has so far been available only for fermion-pair production, with hand-coded amplitudes. We present ACRAIC, an automated, amplitude-level realization of this subtraction for general scattering processes in Sherpa. This method allows us to construct an $\mathcal{O}(\alpha)$ and $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ amplitude level subtraction scheme, in which the infrared-finite remainders are tree-level helicity amplitudes with partition-dependent propagator shifts, computed by the Berends--Giele recursion, and the one-loop electroweak virtual enters through a per-helicity factor from the loop provider. At $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ two independent matchings agree on the size of the missing higher orders to $\sim10^{-3}$, and the estimated perturbative uncertainty shrinks by about an order of magnitude relative to $\mathcal{O}(\alpha)$.

title: A Natural Dark Matter-Dark Energy Interaction from Axion-Monopole Dynamics
summary: We propose a natural framework for interacting dark matter and dark energy based on axion-monopole dynamics in a dark gauge sector. Dark matter is composed of dark 't Hooft-Polyakov monopoles, while dark energy is an ultralight axion whose coupling to the dark gauge field induces an axion-dependent dyon mass through the Witten effect. This generates a direct dark matter-dark energy interaction. We show that generic models with a significant dark matter-dark energy coupling suffer from a naturalness problem: the Coleman-Weinberg potential induced by the interaction is typically much larger than the dark energy scale. In our model, the corrections arise from a monodromy tower of dyon states, allowing them to be exponentially suppressed. In the minimal setup, the interaction strength is predicted to be $\sim 0.1\%$, below the sensitivity of current observations. We discuss scenarios in which cosmological population of higher-charge dyons can enhance the interaction to the percent level, producing an apparent phantom dark energy equation of state. We further show that the parameter space of the axion-monopole model preferred by fitting the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) results can also naturally explain the cosmic birefringence with a small anomaly coefficient.

title: Cosmic birefringence from a stiff axion field and its cosmological implications
summary: We propose a model in which the observed cosmic microwave background birefringence arises from the interaction of photons with a stiff ($w=1$) pseudo-scalar field that today contributes a subdominant fraction of the total energy density, distinct from both dark matter and dark energy. Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constrains the cosmological density of the stiff field, leading to a lower bound for its coupling with photons, $g_{\phi\gamma} > 8.9 \times 10^{-14}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. Photon conversion in cluster-hosted quasars sets an upper bound, $g_{\phi\gamma} < 5.0 \times 10^{-13}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. Therefore, there is a narrow window for the discovery of this cosmological component that can be explored in the forthcoming years with astrophysical axion searches. Moreover, we show that this scenario leads to gravitational-wave signals that can be tested with planned experiments.

title: Self-interacting dark matter from radiative bound-state-formation feedback
summary: Observations of galactic structure motivate sizable dark-matter self-interactions at low velocities, naturally realized through light force mediators. Such mediators can also make inelastic processes very efficient. Unitarity then requires their absorptive contributions to the two-particle self-energy kernel to be resummed, which in turn feeds back into both the elastic and inelastic scattering amplitudes. We study the feedback of radiative bound-state formation on elastic scattering and its implications for self-interacting dark matter. We focus on capture processes through emission of a charged scalar; such transitions are particularly efficient because the scattering and bound states are governed by different effective potentials, a feature also shared by radiative capture through emission of a non-Abelian gauge boson. We show that their feedback can generate sizable elastic scattering relevant for halo dynamics, even when the baseline elastic amplitude vanishes. Notably, the generated elastic cross section can grow toward low velocities, resembling long-range scattering. A companion paper examines the feedback from annihilation processes.

title: Combining Pumping and Absorption Effects in Neutrino Oscillation Probabilities: A Non-Hermitian Framework
summary: We study two-flavour neutrino oscillations in which a coherent off-diagonal interaction from a complex background field coexists with an absorptive channel acting on a single mass eigenstate. Since the two do not commute, the effective Hamiltonian is non-normal and oscillations and damping no longer factorise. We formulate the dynamics both as the no-jump sector of a Lindblad evolution and through biorthogonal diagonalisation, and obtain the evolution operator of our model in closed form. The model interpolates between quasi-global damping, standard invisible decay, and a critical point with polynomial-times-exponential evolution; for initially pure states it describes norm loss rather than decoherence. Comparing neutrinos and antineutrinos in the same background, with the mixing phase $\phi$ reversed and the background phase $\delta$ fixed, we derive closed-form $CP$, $CPT$ and $T$ asymmetries. The $CPT$ asymmetries arise only from this phase assignment. In contrast, the $T$ asymmetry, which is forbidden in unitary two-flavour oscillations, is independent of the prescription: it arises only through the non-normal structure, is proportional to the absorptive coupling, and vanishes only when $\delta+\phi=n\pi$. For equal initial populations the net neutrino--antineutrino asymmetry vanishes identically, while a non-zero flavour asymmetry survives and requires a non-normal Hamiltonian.

title: Two-loop helicity amplitudes for $gg\to W^+W^-$ using high-energy and forward expansions
summary: We calculate next-to-leading order QCD corrections for the process $gg \to W^+W^-$ with two off-shell $W$ bosons, accounting for virtual top quarks in the loop diagrams. Our approach relies on combining expansions valid in different regions of phase space. Specifically, we perform a high-energy expansion in which the Mandelstam variables are much larger than the top-quark mass. Furthermore, we expand around the forward-scattering limit, where the Mandelstam variable $t$ is small. We also provide an expansion for large top-quark mass, which serves as an important cross-check. We provide technical details regarding the various expansions and demonstrate that precise results are obtained for all helicity amplitudes across the entire phase space. Our results exhibit an explicit dependence on all input parameters.

title: This is SParTA: A modular, efficient and scalable transformer architecture for jet-tagging
summary: We present the Sparse Particle-interaction Transformer Architecture (SParTA), a modular, scalable, and efficient transformer for jet tagging at high-energy colliders. Exploiting the steeply falling transverse-momentum ($p_T$) spectrum of jet constituents, SParTA factorizes constituent processing into two topological regimes. Ordered by descending $p_T$, only the $N$ hardest constituents (the hard core) participate in quadratic $O(N^2)$ differential interaction attention driven by pairwise physical and learned relational features. The remaining soft constituents are integrated via linear $O(lN)$ cross-attention to the hard core, preserving soft-radiation and color-flow information while avoiding the $O(l^2)$ memory bottleneck of full self-attention over all $l$ constituents. Pairwise interaction features are computed dynamically in-network from constituent four-momenta and conditioned on global jet-level substructure observables. On the quark-gluon tagging benchmark, a 300K-parameter SParTA model achieves an AUC of 92.02% and accuracy of 85.06%, matching the 2.14M-parameter Particle Transformer (ParT) at one-seventh the parameter count and outperforming IAFormer by 21% in background rejection at 30% signal efficiency. On the boosted top-tagging benchmark, SParTA outperforms ParT and ParticleNet with 511K parameters, while we analyze the architectural trade-offs relative to fully dense multi-layer interaction networks.

title: Illuminating Light Dark Matter with Fixed-Target Experiments
comment: PhD thesis, Chalmers University of Technology, 2026. 148 pages, 34 figures
summary: Astronomical and cosmological observations provide overwhelming evidence for a non-luminous matter component, dark matter (DM), whose particle nature remains unknown. Experimental searches for non-gravitational DM interactions have largely targeted DM with GeV-TeV masses via nuclear recoils, yielding no discovery thus far. DM in the MeV-GeV mass range, however, is theoretically motivated, reproducing the observed relic abundance while remaining invisible to nuclear recoil searches. Such light DM is better probed via electron recoils or at fixed-target experiments. This thesis advances the theoretical and statistical toolkit for light DM searches at fixed-target experiments, spanning model building, statistical inference, global fits, and signal simulation. We survey the landscape of fixed-target searches for light DM, focusing on the Light Dark Matter eXperiment (LDMX). We also simulate DM signatures at the next-generation experiment SHiP to assess its sensitivity. Within minimal DM models, we present a likelihood-based statistical framework for LDMX using the full two-dimensional recoil electron distribution, spanning exclusion, discovery, parameter estimation, and model comparison in frequentist and Bayesian formulations. This establishes the discovery potential of LDMX, and we quantify the direct detection exposure needed to independently confirm a potential signal. Beyond this paradigm, we perform global fits of scalar and fermionic light DM, combining cosmological, astrophysical, and laboratory constraints. We then extend fixed-target searches to spin-1 DM and higher electromagnetic moment dark photons, yielding rich signatures with strong complementarity to other probes. Finally, we go beyond standard nuclear modelling of dark photon production, incorporating elastic nuclear form factors and spectral functions from many-body ab initio methods in place of analytic treatments.

title: Jets as differential probes of hot QCD matter
comment: PhD thesis, Instituto Superior Técnico, Universidade de Lisboa; 248 pages, 48 figures
summary: Ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions create short-lived droplets of deconfined, hot QCD matter whose evolution connects far-from-equilibrium early dynamics to the hydrodynamic quark-gluon plasma. High-energy jets, produced in early hard scatterings and modified by this evolving medium, provide multi-scale probes of its microscopic properties. This thesis develops perturbative QCD tools to extract information about hot QCD matter from its imprint on differential jet substructure observables. Our framework is the BDMPS-Z description of high-energy partons propagating through stochastic colour fields. We first study anisotropic QCD matter by replacing the usual scalar broadening parameter with direction-dependent transverse momentum broadening. This relates anisotropic corrections to medium-induced splittings to spin information and azimuthal patterns in final-state energy flow. Energy correlators are then used as observables sensitive to these effects, including heavy-flavour EECs, azimuthally differential EECs and clover projections designed to isolate leading anisotropy-induced harmonics. We also examine how energy loss affects the interpretation of jet substructure modifications. Quantile matching defines reconstructed energy loss as a population-level shift between vacuum and medium-modified jet spectra. We further develop energy-loss functions, which encode the distribution of energy retained by jet-originated hadrons, and show how their moments enter multi-point projected energy correlators. Finally, we go beyond single $1\to2$ medium-induced splittings by studying spin-induced correlations between successive emissions and higher-point energy correlators including contributions from medium response. The results show that differential jet substructure can probe directional properties of QCD matter and multi-point dynamics of jets propagating through it.

title: Correlations in oscillation data and their impact on neutrino mixing models
comment: 28 pages, 11 figures, 4 tables, for the associated starter kit see this https URL
summary: With increasing precision of neutrino experiments, complete correlation among the oscillation parameters will scrutinize theoretical neutrino mass and mixing models. Using available 1D--3D global-fit datasets, we construct a multidimensional $\tilde{\chi}^2$ function that provides a conservative estimate of the full six-dimensional parameter correlations. In our approach, we delineate the model-constrained parameter space by combining the interpolated experimental data with the analytical relations implied by a given mixing scheme. We identify $\tilde{\chi}^2_{\text{min}}$, corresponding to the optimal agreement attainable for parameter points satisfying the model. Applying this framework to several schemes ($\text{TM}_{1,2}$, $\mu1,2$--$\tau1,2$) yields generally better fits for IO than for NO, with the $\mu1$--$\tau1$ scheme under IO providing the best overall fit. While $\mu1,2$--$\tau1,2$ and $\text{TM}_1$ schemes perform significantly better than $\text{TM}_2$, the latter is excluded at $>3\sigma$ C.L. using NuFIT~v6.1 data. We further evaluate the implications of these correlation-respecting constraints on the effective neutrino mass observables relevant to tritium $\beta$-decay ($m_{\beta}$) and neutrinoless double $\beta$-decay ($m_{\beta\beta}$). The proposed approach can be readily extended to test any theoretical framework that predicts algebraic relations among neutrino oscillation parameters, and we provide a GitHub starter kit.

title: Double diffraction production for dipole-dipole scattering at high energies
summary: This paper is a first attempt to describe double diffractive production in dipole-dipole scattering within high energy QCD. Our approach is based on summing large BFKL Pomeron loops, which generate two clusters of hadrons separated by a rapidity gap. Unlike in the BK framework, our approach allows both clusters to carry large masses. We derive the cross section for the production of two such clusters and show that it exhibits geometric scaling. Testing this scaling behaviour against data from high-energy colliders such as the LHC will be a crucial step in establishing whether large Pomeron loops play a major role in high energy QCD dynamics, and in particular in the unitarization of the scattering amplitude.

title: Nonlocality effects on fermions confined within a hard-wall potential
summary: We investigate nonlocality effects on the energy spectrum of spin-$1/2$ fermions confined by hard-wall potentials. Starting from a nonlocal Dirac theory with a modified kinetic term, we formulate the associated field equation in flat spacetime using cylindrical coordinates. By exploiting the eigenvalue spectrum of the squared Dirac operator, the original infinite-order equation is reduced to a finite-order problem. We also show that on the branch continuously connected to the local Dirac theory the nonlocal corrections can be encoded in an effective fermion mass. We then find analytical energy spectra for two confining geometries: a cylindrical hard wall and a quantum ring defined by two concentric cylindrical boundaries. In both cases, the radial equations reduce to Bessel equations and the boundary conditions quantize the allowed modes. The local hard-wall spectra are recovered for $\Lambda\to\infty$, whereas finite nonlocality shifts the mass contribution and, consequently, the particle--antiparticle energy separation. These results provide a direct characterization of nonlocal effects in quantum-confined fermionic systems.

title: The $b\bar{b}c\bar{c}$ Fully Heavy Tetraquark at the LHC and the FCC: Multimodal Fragmentation and Observability
comment: 49 pages, 8 figures, LHAPDF release of the TQ4Qhf1.0 fragmentation-function set with uncertainties at this https URL
summary: We investigate the production of the all-heavy mixed-flavor $b\bar b c\bar c$ tetraquark through a multimodal fragmentation setup combining direct-multiquark and scalar-diquark mechanisms. Standard Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi (DGLAP) evolution is applied while preserving threshold consistency through the Heavy-Flavor NonRelativistic evolution (HF-NRevo) scheme. The resulting fragmentation functions (FFs) are then embedded into hybrid high-energy and collinear factorization at next-to-leading order for semi-inclusive tetraquark-plus-jet production. We compare the two mechanisms through rapidity-separation distributions at the 14 TeV High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) and at the 100 TeV Future Circular Collider (FCC), finding a clear phenomenological preference for the direct-multiquark channel over the scalar-diquark mode. Integrated cross sections and expected event yields provide favorable production-level prospects for future searches at the HL-LHC, with substantially enhanced statistics at FCC energies. These results establish a quantitative connection between microscopic formation mechanisms and the prospective observability of the $b\bar b c\bar c$ tetraquark at present and future hadron colliders.

title: Non-Classicality in $tW$ system via negativity and geometric quantum discord
summary: We perform a phenomenological study of non-classical correlations in the mixed-dimensional qubit-qutrit system realized by leading order $pp\to tW$ production at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV in the leptonic final state. The two missing neutrinos are reconstructed with conditional normalizing flows trained on simulated detector-level objects, and the joint spin density matrix $\rho_{tW}\in\mathcal{H}_2\otimes\mathcal{H}_3$ is obtained in a generalized Bloch representation from the angular distributions of the leptonic decay products. Non-classical correlations are quantified using the Peres--Horodecki negativity and geometric quantum discord. We quantify the correlations at different region of $m_{tW}$ at the reconstruction level within the Standard Model and the impact of two reducible backgrounds viz. $t\bar{t}$ and $WWj$ processes, tagged using boosted decision trees. We further study the behavior of correlations in presence of anomalous chromomagnetic and chromoelectric dipole moments of the top quark. The sensitivity reach of the quantum observables along with polarization and spin correlation parameters are reported for current LHC and future HL-LHC scenario.

title: Flavor decomposition of electromagnetic multipole moments in $[q_1q_2][\bar q_3 \bar c]$ tetraquarks: Light-quark analogs of $T_{cs1}(2900)^0$ with $J^P = 1^+$
comment: 12 pages, 5 tables,1 figure. The version is accepted for publication in Physics Letters B
summary: We present a systematic study of the magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole moments of compact $[q_1 q_2][\bar q_3 \bar c]$ tetraquark states with quantum numbers $J^P = 1^+$, in the diquark--antidiquark picture and within the light-cone QCD sum rule framework. By performing a flavor decomposition across all admissible $u/d$ configurations, we show that the charm-quark contribution to the electromagnetic moments vanishes algebraically at the operator level -- a structural feature of the specific spin organization adopted here, in which the heavy antiquark resides in a pseudoscalar antidiquark, distinct from the dynamical $1/m_c$ suppression operative in alternative compact constructions and in hadronic molecules. The magnetic moments follow a coherent light-flavor pattern -- positive for $uu$-, negative for $dd$-, and suppressed for mixed-flavor diquarks -- and the quadrupole moments are non-zero throughout, corresponding, in the customary geometrical interpretation, to intrinsically deformed charge distributions. We further identify the dimensionless multipole ratio $\mathcal{D}/\mu$ as a structural observable, independent of the normalization of the interpolating current, which probes the relative geometry of the spin-current and charge distributions complementary to the absolute moments. Taken together, the algebraic decoupling of the charm contribution and the operator-level distinction it implies among different singly-heavy tetraquark architectures constitute methodological signatures that discriminate among the corresponding internal organizations and, to the extent that a physical candidate is dominated by one of them, among compact and molecular interpretations.

title: Matrix divisors, Christoffel transformations and symmetric $d$-connections
summary: The Christoffel transformation $w(x)\mapsto x^2w(x)$ relates elementary bundle modifications to gap probability recurrences. The moment matrix determines normalization and the splitting type. We define the source and target moduli problems by their local data. The modifications identify common stable loci and conjugate their point-addition maps. For Pearson ratios $d(-z-1)/d(z)$ with $°d=1,2$, we construct rational spectral coordinates and compute the induced transformation. For positive even weights with finite moments, reweighting configurations yields the transformed gap probability recurrence. Its coefficient is a rational function of the transformed spectral coordinates. A local formula applies outside these charts under the stated hypotheses.

title: Mapping AdS$_4$ quantum gravity via the Bethe Ansatz formula
summary: The topologically twisted index of 3d ADHM theory can be written as a sum over solutions to the Bethe Ansatz Equations (BAEs) of the XXZ-type model constructed from quantum toroidal $\mathfrak{g}\mathfrak{l}_1$. Via a novel numerical algorithm, we solve for all $p(N)$ physical solutions at $N\leq 21$, where $p(N)$ denotes the number of integer partitions of $N$. Surveying these solutions, we find that in addition to the known "1-cut" solution dual to dyonic black holes, where the gauge holonomies are distributed along a single curve in the complex plane, there are "dressed" 1-cut solutions dual to combined configurations of the black hole and M2-branes, $m$-cut solutions dual to $\mathbb{Z}_m$ orbifolds of the black hole, a discrete family of solutions interpolating between the 1-cut and 3-cut solutions, together with other exotic solutions, at each value of $N$. The free energy of the interpolating solutions cannot be matched with the on-shell action of any known bulk solution. The $1,2,3$-cut solutions and interpolating solutions all have a well-defined large $N$ limit, and their leading order distribution of gauge holonomies can be computed analytically. Whenever possible, we fit the contributions of the solutions to the index to all orders in the $1/N$ expansion with high-precision numerics, and extract the leading non-perturbative correction. With exceptions, these are matched with the results of equivariant localization in the bulk, and the action of wrapped M2-branes respectively.

title: Pfaffian solutions to the Ernst equation
summary: We show that the Yamazaki-Hori solution to the Ernst equation can be represented in the Pfaffian form. We also discuss the consequences of this result for Nakamura's conjecture on the relation between the Ernst equation and the 2D Toda model.

title: Learning the open string spectrum with neural networks
comment: 44 pages, 13 figures, 1 Wolfram notebook attached with a custom made neural network
summary: The tree-level open superstring has an integer mass-squared spectrum on linear Regge trajectories. To what extent is this fixed by consistency conditions: locality, analyticity, crossing, unitarity together with the requirement that $2\to2$ scattering minimize the entanglement it generates? Using the local two-channel crossing symmetric dispersion relation with one-parameter ambiguity ($\lambda$-CSDR) we set up a bootstrap treating both the mass-squared spectrum and the partial-wave coefficients as unknowns which lets the machine learning algorithm to learn the mass-squared spectrum and partial-wave coefficients simultaneously, going beyond earlier work in which the spectrum was fixed. Using the local three-channel crossing symmetric dispersion relation with one-parameter ambiguity we obtain, within the class of amplitudes with soft Regge behavior and infinite higher-spin tower, a bound on the leading Wilson coefficients that we compare with existing bounds and trace to spin-0 dominance. We locate the Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude in the allowed region of the Wilson coefficients space. For amplitudes with two-channel crossing symmetry we find that a Non-dual amplitude exhibits a Polchinski-Strassler type transition from Regge to power-law behavior.

title: Free-field realizations of $\mathcal{N} = 1$ supersymmetric $\mathcal{W}$-algebras associated with Lie superalgebras $B (n - 1 , n)$ and $B (n , n)$
summary: We extend the recursive construction of free-field realizations proposed by Ide, Ito, and Miyazaki to the $\mathcal{N} = 1$ supersymmetric $\mathcal{W}$-algebras $\mathcal{SW} B (n - 1 , n)$ and $\mathcal{SW} B (n , n)$, associated with the Lie superalgebras $B (n - 1 , n)$ and $B (n , n)$, respectively. We obtain explicit free-field realizations of $\mathcal{SW} B (0 , 1)$, $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 1)$, $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 2)$, and $\mathcal{SW} B (2 , 2)$. In particular, the realizations of $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 2)$ and $\mathcal{SW} B (2 , 2)$ are new. Using these realizations, we compute central charges, conformal weights, and eigenvalues of the generating currents on free-field highest-weight states, and construct the local integrals of motion $I_1$, $I_3$, and $I_5$.

title: Surface defects on lens space and transfer matrices
summary: We study surface defects in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ theories of class $\mathcal{S}$ and $\mathcal{N}=1$ theories of class $\mathcal{S}_k$ placed on $L(r,1)\times S^1$. The lens space index depends on the fugacities $p$ and $q$, and the effect of the defects on it is captured by difference operators acting on the fugacities and holonomies of flavor symmetries. For theories of type $A_1$ we determine in closed form the difference operators for the basic defects, labeled by $p^r$, $q^r$ and $pq$, and show that for odd $r$ there exist additional elementary defects, whose operators shift the holonomy by one half modulo $r$. All the operators commute, and the elementary operators generate the others. For even $r$ the same holds once the holonomy is extended to a twisted sector. We show that the elementary operators are traces of $L$-operators whose entries generate a Sklyanin algebra, with nome $q^r$ and shift $pq$. The lens space enters only through the parameters of the algebra and through its representation, which is realized on a doubled holonomy label. The $p$- and $q$-type algebras form a lens space version of the elliptic modular double. For class $\mathcal{S}_k$ theories we propose, and test in several ways, that the defect operators are transfer matrices of inhomogeneous spin chains built from these $L$-operators. Throughout, we use the TQFT structure of the lens space index, which follows from S-duality, both to fix and to check the operators.

title: Towards differential expansion for generic representations
summary: We report the first results of phenomenological analysis, based on extended set of explicitly calculated colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials in \cite{knotebook}. They concern differential expansion (DE), which separates the dependencies on the knot ${\cal K}$ and the representation $R$. %of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials. DE is well understood for symmetric and rectangular representations, while for non-rectangular $R$ even the knot-independent basis $Z_R^X$ of DE is not known. We concentrate on two issues: the possible derivation of DE and on improved characteristic of its defect. We discuss how evolution families -- twist knots, double braids and 3-pretzels -- can be used to find DE by a peculiar triangular transformation of evolution coefficients. Once $Z^R_X$ are found for particular family, they are expected to stay basically the same for arbitrary knots -- modulo controllable reductions, characterized by the defect of DE, which puts knots into different universality classes. Contrary to original expectation, these classes appear labeled not by a single number $\delta^{\cal K}$, but by a whole non-decreasing sequence $\{k_j\}$, which is squeezed between two staircases, ${\rm entier}\left(\frac{j-1}{\delta+1}\right)\leq k_j\leq{\rm entier}\left(\frac{j-1}{{\rm deg}\,\Delta}\right)$, where the upper bound involves Alexander polynomial $\Delta(q^2)$ and follows from the continuation of the Melvin--Morton--Rozansky-Kashaev limit to $A=q^{-m}$ with $m>0$, when the limit gives a {\it positive} power of Alexander. The old assumption $\delta+1={\rm deg}\,\Delta$ is oversimplified and fails for 19 non-alternating knots with 11 and 12 crossings. Last, we list the differences of non-rectangularly colored HOMFLY for various mutant pairs to demonstrate their universality (knot-independence) and nice consistency with the spirit of DE.

title: An Algebraic Formulation of Thermality in Nested Rindler Wedges
summary: Padmanabhan and Kolekar had demonstrated the phenomenon of recursive thermality in two dimensional free field theories where the Rindler vacuum appears thermal to an observer accelerated with respect to the Rindler observer. We study the same construction at an algebraic level for conformal field theories. At each step, a parent wedge is conformally mapped to a reference Minkowski spacetime, where a new right Rindler wedge and its left sibling are selected. We illustrate that under the Bisognano--Wichmann property, thermality holds at every generation: the state associated with a parent wedge becomes a KMS state when restricted to its right child. Further, using the modular structure of the wedge and its causal sibling, we identify the sibling algebra with the modular commutant and derive the corresponding recursive modular flow explicitly.

title: Nambu-Goldstone Bosons and Quantum Fisher Information
summary: The quantum Fisher matrix and geometric tensor are powerful tools for quantifying the nature of quantum systems. Unfortunately, the formalism needed to compute these quantities is opaque and has limited the development of physical intuition for their behavior, even in the ground state. For quantum systems with continuous symmetries, we know the ground state can be understood in a model-independent and intuitive way from the correlation functions of conserved currents and charges. In this paper, we demonstrate an equivalence between the quantum Fisher matrix associated with the ground states of systems with continuous symmetries and the Nambu-Goldstone. bosons produced by broken generators. We will show that the information metric defined by the Fisher matrix is the same as the Zamolodchikov metric that defines the coset space of the system. Next we show that the Uhlmann curvature associated with multi-parameter estimation is the same as the charge density matrix that defines the difference between type-A and type-B Nambu-Goldstone bosons. We demonstrate these connections in several examples and discuss the generalization to finite temperature.

title: Scale-separated AdS vacua on Riemann-Flat Manifolds
summary: Supergravity compactifications supported by fluxes and Casimir energy offer a simple strategy to concoct explicit, controlled and isolated vacua with parametric scale separation and soft supersymmetry breaking. Exploiting the special properties of both the Casimir and flux potentials with respect to Laplacian operators in moduli space, we prove that the simplest such class of solutions, given by toroidal compactifications of eleven-dimensional supergravity threaded by any fluxes, always exhibit perturbative instabilities in the form of tachyonic modes below the BF bound. This no-go theorem applies to any toroidal supergravity compactification supported by $p$-form fluxes. We also study compactifications on more general Riemann-flat manifolds (RFM's). Concretely, we find a tachyon-free AdS$_4$ vacuum by compactifying M-Theory on a $T^7/\mathbb{Z}_2^3$. This constitutes the first ever example of a fully top-down, perturbatively stable, scale-separated AdS without localized sources.

title: Bilocal flows and universality with field-dependent regulators
summary: Many functional renormalization group flows employ a regulator that depends on the fields, as in proper-time and spectrally adjusted flows and in background-independent formulations of gauge theories and quantum gravity. Such a regulator generates additional terms in the flow, and their omission may spoil universality. We introduce bilocal flows, in which the effective action depends on the field and on the cutoff kernel as independent variables. The construction identifies the additional terms, and an exact sum rule shows that the first nontrivial coefficient of the anomalous dimension coincides with that of a fixed-regulator flow for every admissible regulator profile, so that universality is restored. For massless $\lambda\phi^4$ theory with a proper-time regulator, the reduced flow gives a profile-dependent anomalous dimension, while the completed flow gives the universal two-loop coefficient $C_\eta=1/6$ for every profile.

title: Deconfinement on $\mathbb{Z}_{F}$ and Axion Domain Walls
summary: We investigate the nontrivial dynamics on $\mathbb{Z}_{F}$ domain walls and compute their tension in quantum chromodynamics (QCD) compactified on a circle with $N$ colors and $F < N$ massless fundamental flavors. In the process, we obtain insights on the $\eta'$ meson's potential in a regime where it is heavy and comparable in mass to other QCD resonances, as in Nature. We employ a center-stabilized compactification of QCD on a small circle of size $L$ with color-flavor twisted boundary conditions for the quarks. We demonstrate that probe particles in color representations of $N$-ality $N/\mathrm{gcd}(N,F)$ are deconfined on the $\mathbb{Z}_{F}$ domain walls whenever $N$ and $F$ are not coprime. This is reminiscent of deconfinement on axion domain walls in pure Yang--Mills. Finally, in the double scaling limit $N\rightarrow \infty$ keeping $NL$ and $F$ fixed, the infrared spectrum spans an emergent dimension. We establish that the $\mathbb{Z}_{F}$ domain walls are dual to electrostatic charge distributions in this emergent dimension. This duality allows us to compute their tension analytically and find a different tension scaling at large-$N$ between $\mathbb{Z}_{F}$ domain walls in QCD and axion domain walls in pure Yang--Mills, in center-stabilized compactifications.

title: Gravitational Path Integral and String Theory
summary: Gravitational path integral has had many applications in recent years. Using the example of supersymmetric index, which provides one of the most controlled tests of gravitational path integral, we argue that even in this controlled case, naive gravitational path integral cannot produce consistent results beyond low orders. However one can go further using stringy inputs, e.g. the choice of UV cut-off and the choice of correct path integration variable, without having to do full fledged string calculation. We also discuss to what extent we are led to string scale UV cut-off even if we begin with a supergravity theory without an a priori bias towards string theory. This is a review of mostly published results, but we clarify several details.

title: Information Geometry of DGLAP Evolution: From Geodesic Tests to Emergent Small-Circle Geometry
summary: We investigate the geometric structure of leading-order (LO) nonsinglet DGLAP evolution on the Fisher--Rao manifold of normalized valence distributions, asking whether the QCD-selected trajectory is geodesic and how its departure from geodesic motion is organized. Through the isometric embedding $\Phi=2\sqrt{p}$, the evolution is represented as a curve on a Hilbert sphere of radius two, with its velocity and acceleration determined directly by the DGLAP operator. For a GRV98-based total-valence trajectory over $2\leq Q^2\leq 2000~{\rm GeV}^2$, we find a nonzero but weakly scale-dependent geodesic curvature. An arc-length-weighted principal-component analysis shows that two affine directions capture more than $99.999\%$ of the trajectory variance. The corresponding affine plane intersects the Fisher sphere in a small circle, whose predicted geodesic curvature closely agrees with that reconstructed from the DGLAP-generated acceleration. An $x$-resolved analysis further reveals that Fisher motion is governed by relative PDF reshaping rather than probability weight alone, with different momentum-fraction regions contributing to motion along the trajectory and its transverse bending. The Mellin representation provides a complementary perspective on the effective dimensional reduction through the collective evolution of the spectral hierarchy. These results establish a quantitative information-geometric characterization of the reference LO DGLAP trajectory and reveal an organized, near-small-circle structure over the finite evolution interval.

title: Pion chemical potentials as seen from transverse momentum distributions
summary: We examine the transverse momentum spectra of negatively charged pions emitted in proton-proton, proton-antiproton, and nucleus-nucleus collisions at beam momenta from tens to hundreds of GeV$/c$. The measured spectra are described within the framework of nonextensive Tsallis statistics, allowing the corresponding chemical potentials to be determined through a quantitative comparison with experimental data. The extracted thermodynamic parameters are subsequently employed to explore the structure of the phase diagram in the chemical potential-temperature ($\mu$-$T$) plane, with particular emphasis on identifying possible signatures of a phase transition. Within this interpretation, pion production in the midrapidity region is associated with a phase characterized by broken chiral symmetry, whereas increasing rapidity corresponds to an evolution toward a regime in which chiral symmetry is restored.

title: From Harmonic Oscillators to Multiplicity Distributions in Particle Production Processes
summary: We propose an oscillator framework of studying multi-particle production processes using the information theory approach. For a system of degenerate oscillators, we derive the negative binomial distribution (NBD) and its nonadditive generalization represented as gNBD. We observe that gNBD derived from nonadditive statistics describes data in higher multiplicity region, thereby providing an alternative for the multi-component distributions used in phenomenological studies. We also generalize our framework for non-degenerate oscillators and encounter a Lerch-type generalization of the Barnes zeta function that, to the best of our knowledge, has not been studied in the context of nonadditive statistics and multiplicity studies before.

title: Displaced e+e- Signatures from an X17-Mediated Inelastic Dark-Sector Cascade
summary: We investigate displaced electron-positron signatures from an inelastic dark sector mediated by a light vector boson associated with the X17 anomaly. A heavy neutral fermion decays into a lighter stable state and the mediator, whose subsequent decay produces a single visible vertex after two stages of neutral propagation. We calculate the decay width, displacement distribution, lepton kinematics, and production rate in electro-positron collisions, including vector polarization. At Belle II, stronger dark-sector couplings increase production but require finely adjusted masses to preserve a macroscopic decay length. We quantify off-shell contributions and assess the validity of the two-body approximation. We show that the electron-positron pair cannot satisfy simultaneously the moment and opening-angle cuts of an existing search proposal for the configuration studied. Less restrictive selections allow nonzero kinematic acceptance. Our results clarify the experimental requirements for searching these signatures at Belle II.

title: Partial reconstruction of the decay $B_{s}^{0}\rightarrow ϕ(K^{+}K^{-})η' (π^{+}π^{-}η)$
summary: The decay $B_s^0 \to \phi(K^+K^-)\eta'(\pi^+\pi^-\eta)$ is of particular interest in flavour physics because in the Standard Model it proceeds predominantly through the quark transition $\bar{b} \to \bar{s}s\bar{s}$. However, the reconstruction of this decay is experimentally challenging due to the presence of the neutral $\eta$ particle, which significantly reduces the overall reconstruction efficiency. In this study, the feasibility of using the partial reconstruction technique to reconstruct the invariant mass of the $B_s^0$ meson without explicitly detecting the $\eta$ particle is investigated. Monte Carlo simulated events corresponding to an FCC-ee environment are used, and the effects of detector momentum and vertex resolutions on the reconstruction performance are examined. The results show that improved vertex resolution substantially improves the global reconstructed mass response and partial-reconstruction efficiency, while improvements in momentum resolution are manifested primarily through a narrowing of the fitted central DCB component. These findings suggest that future high-luminosity $e^+e^-$ colliders such as FCC-ee could effectively exploit the partial reconstruction technique to study rare decay modes containing undetected neutral particles.

title: Two-Component Dark Matter and Strongly First-Order Electroweak Phase Transition via a Two-Step Mechanism in the Inert Doublet plus Real Singlet Model
summary: We study a two-component dark matter model in which a real singlet scalar and an inert doublet scalar are simultaneously present alongside the Standard Model, each stabilized by an independent discrete symmetry. The real singlet undergoes a strong first-order transition at high temperature, establishing an intermediate phase with a non-zero singlet vacuum expectation value, which in turn generates the barrier required for the Higgs field to complete a strongly first-order electroweak transition at a lower temperature. This two-step mechanism naturally enforces the condition $v_c/T_c \geq 1$, the sphaleron washout-avoidance criterion necessary for electroweak baryogenesis. The gravitational wave spectrum from both steps is computed; the second step produces a decihertz signal, peaking near $0.08$--$0.34~\mathrm{Hz}$ across the viable parameter space and $0.14$--$0.22~\mathrm{Hz}$ at the benchmark points, that reaches the sensitivity of DECIGO for the strongest transitions and of BBO more widely, while the first remains sub-threshold for all planned detectors. At the coupling values required to drive the phase transition, the singlet is generically underabundant as a thermal relic, so the inert doublet carries the dominant fraction of the observed relic density. Confronting the model with current constraints, we find that the LUX-ZEPLIN 2024 result excludes the entire electroweak-phase-transition-viable parameter space of the singlet sector across the full mass range, even after rescaling by the singlet relic fraction, establishing a complete no-go for the singlet as a viable thermal dark matter candidate in this framework.

title: Femtoscopic correlation functions between the lightest charmed hadrons
summary: Femtoscopic momentum correlations probe low-energy interactions of short-lived charmed hadrons that are inaccessible to conventional scattering experiments. We calculate the correlation functions of $D^{+}D^{+}$, $D^{0}D^{0}$, $D^{+}D^{0}$, and $\Lambda_c^+\Lambda_c^+$ in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.02$~TeV, using species-dependent non-Gaussian PHSD sources constructed from hadronization points and strong interactions calibrated to lattice-QCD scattering lengths: OBE and EFT-contact models for $DD$, and an EFT-contact model for $\Lambda_c\Lambda_c$. Coulomb and quantum-statistical effects are included consistently. Although the calibrated interactions are weakly repulsive, the channels separate the relevant effects: $D^{+}D^{0}$, free of Coulomb distortion and identical-particle interference, gives the cleanest access to the $DD$ strong interaction, whereas $\Lambda_c^+\Lambda_c^+$ is most pronounced in peripheral collisions, where the compact source enhances the low-momentum signal. The $\Lambda_c\Lambda_c$ input is taken from lattice QCD at a nonphysical pion mass, so its physical-point shift is not quantified here. Within these stated inputs, the results provide ALICE-ready benchmark correlations and background references; the quoted bands propagate only the lattice scattering-length uncertainty.

title: Information geometry of DGLAP evolution
comment: 28 pages, 2 figures, 6 tables. Supplemental material (14 pages, 1 figure) and the program codes and stored outputs that reproduce every number in the paper
summary: Quark and gluon splittings shift proton momentum toward smaller fractions with increasing resolution. Momentum conservation makes the summed momentum-weighted quark and gluon densities, when nonnegative, a probability distribution. We apply information geometry, the geometry of probability distributions, to this probabilistic form of Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi evolution. We evaluate, to our knowledge for the first time, the speed at which the shape of the proton's momentum distribution changes, measured by how well distributions at neighboring resolutions can be told apart statistically. At leading order, with one-loop splitting functions and running coupling, five fixed quark flavors, nonnegative quark and gluon densities and sufficiently regular inputs, we obtain a closed-form lower bound on this speed. Once the coupling is specified, three numbers of the input (the distribution at the starting resolution) fix the bound at every scale without computing the evolved distribution. For three of the five model inputs at four scales from 2 GeV to 10 TeV, the squared bound is at least 94.8 percent of the squared speed. The bound is reached when the distribution's relative rate of change is linear in the logarithm of the inverse momentum fraction. For these three model inputs at the four scales, the relative rate of change is close to this linear form in mean square weighted by momentum.

title: Form factors and weak decays of $Λ_b\toΛ_c^*(2595)$ and $Ξ_b\toΞ_c^*(2790)$
A Catalog of Lepton Mass Textures from Koide and Alikhanov Relations
comment: 21 pages + references; 3 figures and 12 tables. Comments are welcome!
summary: The empirical Koide relation for charged-lepton masses and the recently proposed Alikhanov relation for neutrino mass-squared differences offer intriguing hints toward understanding the structure of lepton mass matrices. Motivated by these observations, we systematically explore charged-lepton and neutrino mass-matrix textures that satisfy these relations and confront their predictions for lepton mixing with experimental data. For the charged-lepton sector, we investigate representative positive Hermitian square-root matrices classified by the number of common eigenvector directions of their generators: three, one, or none. For the neutrino sector, an exhaustive enumeration of real symmetric integer matrices with entries between $-5$ and $5$ identifies six signed-permutation classes with $m_1=0$ and six with $m_1>0$ that satisfy the Alikhanov relation. Combining these neutrino textures with the charged-lepton constructions, allowing for different relative flavor orientations and phase alignments, yields $400$ viable structural pairs consistent with the measured lepton mixing parameters. All retained solutions satisfy the adopted cosmological bound on the sum of neutrino masses and existing laboratory constraints. In particular, the full-rank neutrino textures predict $m_1\simeq16.77$-$17.22\,\mathrm{meV}$. Representative viable solutions yield effective Majorana masses $m_{\beta\beta}\simeq1.29$-$4.03\,\mathrm{meV}$ and $4.07$-$18.67\,\mathrm{meV}$ for the $m_1=0$ and $m_1>0$ branches, respectively, providing potential targets for future high-sensitivity searches.

title: Polarization signatures of mixed scalar - pseudoscalar ALP - photon couplings in intense laser pulses
summary: We investigate photon-to-axion-like-particle (ALP) conversion in a finite, linearly polarized laser pulse for a single ALP field with simultaneous scalar-type and pseudoscalar-type couplings to photons. Varying the collision angle between the strong pulse and the probe provides a continuous kinematic scan of the resonant ALP mass. For fixed kinematics in this setting, the scalar-type and pseudoscalar-type ALP conversion amplitudes interfere coherently, making both the photon-to-ALP conversion probability and the polarization rotation depend on the difference between the probe polarization angle $\alpha$ and the coupling angle $\theta_g$. Conversion is maximal at $|\alpha-\theta_g|=90^\circ$, where the polarization rotation vanishes, while the rotation magnitude peaks at $\alpha-\theta_g=45^\circ$ modulo $90^\circ$, where conversion is half-maximal. These complementary polarization-angle dependences provide polarization-resolved signatures of mixed scalar--pseudoscalar photon couplings.

title: Probing the $τ$ anomalous magnetic and electric dipole moments in photon-induced $γγ\toτ^+τ^-$ production at the FCC-hh
summary: The sensitivity of the FCC-hh to the anomalous magnetic moment $a_\tau$ and the electric dipole moment $d_\tau$ of the $\tau$ lepton is studied in photon-induced $\gamma\gamma\to\tau^+\tau^-$ production with both $\tau$ leptons decaying hadronically. Central exclusive (elastic) signal events, in which both protons remain intact, are generated with MadGraph5_aMC@NLO using a FeynRules UFO model of the anomalous $\gamma\tau\tau$ vertex merged with the TauDecay model, so that the $\tau$ decays and their spin correlations are included in the matrix element. Single- and double-dissociative production is estimated with SuperChic and added to the elastic signal with its own coupling dependence and with normalisation and shape uncertainties of 25%. Pythia 8 decays the unstable hadrons in the signal, decays the $\tau$ leptons and simulates the parton shower and hadronisation in the backgrounds, and hadronises the dissociated protons. Signal and backgrounds are passed through the Delphes simulation of the FCC-hh detector. Hadronic $\tau$ decays are reconstructed from particle-flow tracks and photons with an algorithm based on the hadrons-plus-strips approach, with an efficiency of 73.4% within the acceptance. Requiring no additional tracks from the $\tau$ vertices retains part of the dissociative contribution and reduces the Drell-Yan and $\gamma\gamma\to WW$ backgrounds to 0.9% of the SM yield. The couplings are constrained from the shape of the total transverse mass distribution. For a centre-of-mass energy of 84 TeV and 30 ab$^{-1}$, the expected 95% CL limits are $-3.38\times10^{-4} < a_\tau < 3.36\times10^{-4}$ and $|d_\tau| < 1.88\times10^{-18}\,e\,$cm, about an order of magnitude beyond the current bounds. Results are also given for FCC-hh scenarios between 72 and 120 TeV and for an optimistic detector parametrisation.

title: Soft Breaking Naturalness in Majorana Fermion Loop induced Scalar and Majoron Amplitudes
summary: Majorana fermion loops contribute a shift-symmetry violating effective potential to the coupled scalar field. When the Majorana fermion is light, a larger number of symmetry violating insertions let the loop contribution to grow increasingly infrared sensitive to the Majorana mass. With explicit calculations, we calculate the symmetry violating amplitudes, show that the scalar potential's natural scales serve as nonzero kinematic matching points which remove the superficial sensitivity to the symmetry-violating Majorana mass, continuously restoring the shift symmetry in agreement with 't Hooft naturalness. In the spontaneous broken phase, the scalar radial vacuum expectation value readily ensures the infrared safety of symmetry violating Majorana fermion loops, and all $n$-point Majoron functions develop a leading linear dependence on the symmetry violating parameter in the soft breaking limit, which matches the expansion of the Coleman-Weinberg determinant.

title: Classical solitons in anti-self-dual Yang-Mills theory
summary: We study classical soliton solutions in split-signature anti-self-dual Yang-Mills theory. Using Zakharov's dressing method, we construct rational lump solitons, which are localised near two-dimensional surfaces, and wall solitons, which have codimension one. We further describe multi-phase solutions which have multiple walls meeting at trivalent junctions and form four-dimensional foam-like structures. Two-pole solutions describe soliton interactions and we find non-trivial colour-dressed phase shifts for wall interactions. We consider the four-dimensional analogue of Ward's lump scattering for the restricted kinematics of coincident poles and show that there are non-trivial interactions in the collinear limit. Finally, we show that the determinant of the soliton matrix provides a $\tau$-function which acts as a potential for gauge-invariant scalar quantities such as the Yang-Mills Lagrangian density.

title: Flux Vacua, Asymptotic Periods, and Relatively Anosov Representations
summary: We develop a topological method to detect classical flux vacua of M-theory on Calabi-Yau fourfolds with a single complex structure modulus using only asymptotic period data and monodromy information. To this end, we express the index of the F-term of the flux superpotential as a winding number along the boundary of the universal cover of the complex structure moduli space. The index evaluates to a sum over zeros and poles of a suitably normalized boundary F-term, where local contributions can be computed algebraically on a dense set of boundary points. Assuming a conjectured bound on the remaining contributions, sufficiently many sign changes of the boundary F-term guarantee a flux vacuum in the interior. We illustrate the method on the mirror Fermat sextic with explicit examples and a systematic flux scan. A main technical ingredient in our construction is a continuity result for projective period maps: we prove that the non-holomorphic (3,1)-period map extends continuously to the boundary of the covering space if the monodromy representation is relatively Anosov. In general, this property does not hold for holomorphic (4,0)-periods.

title: IR extremality and UV softness in string bootstrap
summary: Whether string amplitudes can be characterized by extremality within the space of consistent S-matrices is an intriguing question. We address this question within the framework of positivity bootstrap. We compute positivity bounds by minimizing the $F^4$ Wilson coefficient while fixing subleading coefficients, and show that the Veneziano amplitude lies close to the boundary of the allowed region. However, this numerical proximity does not imply exact extremality, as demonstrated by explicit counterexamples. When additional KLT-motivated UV softness is imposed, the Veneziano amplitude is found to uniquely minimize the $F^4$ coefficient for $4\leq D\leq10$, connecting the extremality of the Veneziano amplitude to its stringy UV behavior and offering a new perspective on what makes string theory special.

title: AdS$_2$ from Type IIA on weak G$_2$ manifolds
summary: We present and study supersymmetric warped ${\rm AdS}_2 \times {\rm M}_7 \times I$ solutions of Type IIA supergravity, where M$_7$ is a weak G$_2$ holonomy manifold. Locally, the solutions are characterized by a cubic polynomial. We distinguish two branches, Branch 1 and Branch 2, and analyze their global properties, taking flux quantization into account. At the endpoints of the interval $I$ they exhibit either OF1-plane or O8/D8 type of singularities with Branch 1 allowing also for a Spin(7) cone. In the case of zero Romans mass, Branch 1 uplifts to eleven dimensions to ${\rm AdS}_4 \times {\rm M}_7$ whereas Branch 2 uplifts to warped ${\rm AdS}_3 \times {\rm M}_7 \times I$ with OM2-plane type of singularities.

title: Mapping AdS$_4$ quantum gravity via the Bethe Ansatz formula
summary: The topologically twisted index of 3d ADHM theory can be written as a sum over solutions to the Bethe Ansatz Equations (BAEs) of the XXZ-type model constructed from quantum toroidal $\mathfrak{g}\mathfrak{l}_1$. Via a novel numerical algorithm, we solve for all $p(N)$ physical solutions at $N\leq 21$, where $p(N)$ denotes the number of integer partitions of $N$. Surveying these solutions, we find that in addition to the known "1-cut" solution dual to dyonic black holes, where the gauge holonomies are distributed along a single curve in the complex plane, there are "dressed" 1-cut solutions dual to combined configurations of the black hole and M2-branes, $m$-cut solutions dual to $\mathbb{Z}_m$ orbifolds of the black hole, a discrete family of solutions interpolating between the 1-cut and 3-cut solutions, together with other exotic solutions, at each value of $N$. The free energy of the interpolating solutions cannot be matched with the on-shell action of any known bulk solution. The $1,2,3$-cut solutions and interpolating solutions all have a well-defined large $N$ limit, and their leading order distribution of gauge holonomies can be computed analytically. Whenever possible, we fit the contributions of the solutions to the index to all orders in the $1/N$ expansion with high-precision numerics, and extract the leading non-perturbative correction. With exceptions, these are matched with the results of equivariant localization in the bulk, and the action of wrapped M2-branes respectively.

title: A group theoretic calculation of multi-invariants of some stabilizer states
summary: We study multi-invariants---a multi-partite generalization of Renyi entropies---of simple stabilizer states, for an arbitrary replica symmetry group. We develop a group theoretic technique for evaluating such invariants, which operates on the replica group and involves counting intersections among its cosets. Our techniques streamline the calculations of multi-invariants for graph states with two GHZ-like nodes and for certain generalizations thereof. The methodology developed here is most suitable when the quantum state is simple but flexibility over the replica group is desired.

title: Realization of de Sitter spacetime in AdS/CFT
summary: We construct horizonless, everywhere-regular solitons containing a de~Sitter core inside an asymptotically anti--de~Sitter spacetime, using an ordinary action of Einstein gravity, a Maxwell field, and a charged scalar. The object is a gravitating gauged $Q$-ball whose false-vacuum interior acts as a positive effective cosmological constant, sourcing an inner de~Sitter region joined through a thin wall to a charged, asymptotically AdS exterior. Two general requirements are emphasized: the scalar must lie in a near-false-vacuum (slow-roll--like) regime, and the exterior is driven to the extremal Reissner--Nordström--AdS locus in the thin-wall limit, in which the wall approaches the common would-be horizon. Since the solution is static and spherically symmetric, it may correspond to a semiclassical charge-$Q$ state of the dual CFT, realizing de~Sitter space approximately within a holographic theory. We also discuss free fluctuations whose de~Sitter--core modes appear as parametrically low-lying excitations above the state, bulk reconstruction, and the near-extremal regime, where finite-${\mathcal N}$ effects are expected to cut off the formal classical throat and replace its independent free-field modes by an interacting near-throat sector.

title: Classical and Stochastic Trans-Planckian Censorship
summary: The trans-Planckian censorship conjecture (TCC) limits inflation to a deadline of $N_{\rm TCC}=\ln(M_{\rm Pl}/H_{\rm end})$ e-folds. We formulate it in stochastic inflation as a bound at confidence $1-\delta$ on the probability that a history outlasts the deadline, with three readings: one worldline, the region grown from one Hubble patch, and the reheated volume. Each reading becomes a closed-form condition, rigorous for a linear roll in leading-order stochastic inflation (for the region, in a branching model) and sharp at leading order in $N_{\rm TCC}$: a linear roll whose classical history lasts $N_{\rm cl}$ e-folds respects the TCC if $1-N_{\rm cl}/N_{\rm TCC}\geq\{2\mathcal{P}_\zeta[w+\ln(1/\delta)/N_{\rm TCC}]\}^{1/2}$, with $w=0$ for a worldline and $w=3$ for a region. On a linear slope without vacuum decay, the worldline and region readings are never weaker than the classical TCC, and on the CMB-normalized attractor all readings agree closely with it, so the bounds on the scale of inflation stand. A classical phase that ends in a flat quantum well, which the overdamped classical TCC excludes, is allowed with a margin of a few e-folds per worldline. Near the onset of eternal inflation, the readings differ. On a linear slope, a region must leave the fraction $\sqrt{6\mathcal{P}_\zeta}$ of the deadline unused at leading order: eternal inflation is excluded for every classical history that uses a finite fraction of the deadline, as is a band of non-eternal slopes, and the slope bound becomes $|V'|>V^{3/2}/[\sqrt2\,\pi(1-N_{\rm cl}/N_{\rm TCC})]$. Per worldline, every slope is allowed, given a margin of a few standard deviations. A false vacuum must decay at about the eternal threshold $\Gamma=9H^4/(4\pi)$ or faster for a region or the volume, but only faster than $3H^4\ln(1/\delta)/(4\pi N_{\rm TCC})$ per worldline. Whether the TCC forbids eternal inflation depends on the reading.

title: Pfaffian solutions to the Ernst equation
summary: We show that the Yamazaki-Hori solution to the Ernst equation can be represented in the Pfaffian form. We also discuss the consequences of this result for Nakamura's conjecture on the relation between the Ernst equation and the 2D Toda model.

title: Holographic Reconstruction from Broken Conformal Gauge Symmetry
summary: We investigate bulk--boundary structures in $\AdS_4/\CFT_3$ from the viewpoint of gravity as a broken phase of conformal gauge symmetry. A crucial distinction is made between the Euler and Pontryagin characteristic classes.
